ai.description: *Minervarya kalinga* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and a distinct pale vertebral stripe. It features a sharp snout and granular skin with longitudinal dermal ridges.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya kalinga* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous glandular fold extending from behind the eye to the shoulder, unlike similar species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya kalinga* inhabits moist deciduous forests and agricultural landscapes, typically found near water bodies at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya kalinga* is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in leaf litter or near water bodies during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya kalinga* breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in small, temporary water bodies. Females deposit clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in the water.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya kalinga* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Minervarya kalinga* produces a high-pitched, rapid series of pulsed chirps, often heard emanating from shallow, temporary rain pools or waterlogged paddy fields.
